title: Best intent data tools for B2B sales teams: 5 options compared
summary: Compare 5 intent data tools for B2B sales teams. Review signal sources, pricing requirements and use cases to find the right fit.
body_markdown:
Intent data tools help B2B sales teams find accounts showing relevant research or engagement. Choosing one starts with deciding where you need visibility. Are you interested in research across business websites, activity on software marketplaces, or visits to your own site?


Bombora is worth considering for topic-based research signals. For teams that need intent within a broader account-based sales and marketing program, 6sense and Demandbase are options. G2 Buyer Intent focuses on software evaluation, while HubSpot Buyer Intent lets HubSpot users review website activity and other company signals within their CRM.


Before comparing accounts labeled “in market,” check what each tool observed. Your sellers need to understand the evidence behind a score and what action it supports.


We reviewed official product documentation and commercial information on November 11, 2026. Our recommendations reflect where each tool fits; we have not run a hands-on performance benchmark. Floworks builds Jesse, covered separately below for public company research and contact finding.


## Intent data tools at a glance


Tool Consider it when you need Signal or research focus Check before buying


Bombora Company Surge Topic-based research to inform account prioritization Changes in company research across Bombora’s Data Co-op Whether the topics and account coverage match your market


6sense Intent data connected to account prioritization and sales or marketing workflows Keyword research, website activity, and additional connected signals Which data and workflows your proposed package includes


Demandbase Intent within an account-based sales and marketing program Keyword intent, website engagement, and other account context The scope of the platform or standalone data purchase


G2 Buyer Intent Evidence of software evaluation within relevant categories Product, category, pricing, and competitive research across its marketplace network Signal access for each subscribed product and category


HubSpot Buyer Intent Company intent information within an existing HubSpot setup Website visits, research activity, and company signals Subscription requirements, tracking setup, and credit usage


For background on how these signals work, see our[guide to buyer intent data](https://blog.floworks.ai/buyer-intent-data/) .


## 1. Bombora Company Surge: for topic-based account research


Bombora Company Surge measures company research across its Data Co-op of business publishers, brands, and data providers. It compares recent activity with the account’s past behavior to identify increased interest in particular topics. Bombora also describes persona-level context, including roles and seniority, alongside account-level intent.[Bombora product overview](https://bombora.com/intent/) .


Bombora is worth evaluating if you have a defined target market and need help prioritizing accounts. If you sell cloud security software, check whether its topics let you distinguish relevant security research from general interest in cloud technology.


Use your own account list to review sample output. Check the topic descriptions and observation period, along with the company match, before deciding to reach out. You will still need a conversation to qualify an account researching a problem.


Request a quote for the coverage and delivery you need. Bombora’s Salesforce AppExchange listing advertises a starting price of $5,000 USD per company per year for that offering. That price applies to the listed offering; other Company Surge configurations need their own quote.[Salesforce AppExchange listing](https://appexchange.salesforce.com/appxListingDetail?listingId=a0N3A00000EOCfTUAX&tab=s) .


## 2. 6sense: for connecting intent to account workflows


6sense combines keyword research signals with website activity and other connected sources. Its documentation says anonymous research is matched to an account. To link activity to a named contact, that person must have already identified themselves, and the relevant systems must be connected. 6sense delivers intent data through integrations, APIs, and files.[6sense intent documentation](https://6sense.com/platform/intent-data) .


Consider 6sense if you need to get intent data to sellers and use it to prioritize accounts. In a demo, follow one account from the original signal to the record or list a rep would use. Have the vendor identify any configuration or additional products needed along the way.


You can buy 6sense’s Keyword Intent, Firmographic, and Technographic Data Packs without a full platform subscription. Other data types have different access requirements.[6sense Data Packs](https://6sense.com/platform/data-packs) .


6sense uses customized pricing. Get a quote that specifies the data, users, credits, and workflows you need so you can compare packages on the same terms.[6sense pricing](https://6sense.com/pricing) .


## 3. Demandbase: for account-based sales and marketing programs


Demandbase’s intent documentation covers keyword intent, company information, website engagement, and public content associated with business stakeholders. It describes intent as probabilistic. These signals suggest a potential opportunity; a purchase decision still needs to be confirmed.[Demandbase intent documentation](https://support.demandbase.com/hc/en-us/articles/360056755791-Understanding-Demandbase-Intent) .


Demandbase is worth considering when sales and marketing share an account-based program. During your evaluation, check what happens after a research signal appears. Who receives it, how does it change the account’s treatment, and where does the team record the outcome?


Have the vendor explain which intent comes from Demandbase and which comes from partners. When several sources contribute to a score, sellers need enough context to decide how to follow up.


Demandbase charges a platform fee plus a fee per user for its Sales and Marketing platform. Its Data solutions are also available separately for use in existing systems. Request a quote for the option you plan to use.[Demandbase pricing](https://www.demandbase.com/pricing/) .


## 4. G2 Buyer Intent: for software evaluation signals


G2 Buyer Intent includes research across G2, Capterra, Software Advice, and GetApp. Signals include product profile visits and pricing activity, as well as research into categories and alternatives. Access depends on your subscription. If you need signals for several G2-listed products, each product needs its own subscription.[G2 Buyer Intent documentation](https://documentation.g2.com/docs/buyer-intent) .


G2 is worth evaluating if buyers research your software category on these marketplaces. Review the activity available for your category, including how the account record distinguishes interest in your product from general category research.


A company researching alternatives to another product may deserve a closer look. Check whether it has compared that product directly with yours before choosing a follow-up.


G2’s published plan comparison lists Buyer Intent as an add-on for Professional and Enterprise packages. Get the full price for your products, categories, and required integrations, including the add-on cost beyond the base seller plan.[G2 plans](https://sell.g2.com/plans) .


## 5. HubSpot Buyer Intent: for teams already working in HubSpot


HubSpot Buyer Intent shows company-level website activity, including visits and viewed pages. Its documentation also describes research signals and company news. Website identification uses the HubSpot tracking code to match visits to companies.[HubSpot Buyer Intent documentation](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/reports/use-buyer-intent) .


If you already use HubSpot, start by reviewing the intent information available in your account. Check whether it gives sellers enough context to prioritize companies and which features your subscription includes.


HubSpot also includes Bombora-powered Company Surge signals through company tracking. These are separate from HubSpot’s native research signals. The included Company Surge capability does not require a separate Bombora account.[HubSpot Company Surge documentation](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/reports/use-company-surge-signals-powered-by-bombora) .


Estimate credit usage before turning on ongoing tracking. Adding companies and tracking their signals use credits, and tracking is charged monthly after the initial charge. Work out the cost for the companies you plan to monitor, accounting for subscription and feature requirements too.[HubSpot usage requirements](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/reports/use-buyer-intent) .


## How to compare buyer intent tools before signing


Give every vendor the same market and sales problem to work with. This makes it easier to compare their output. Broad topic coverage in one demo is hard to assess against a carefully selected account with unusually clear activity in another.


Start with your[ideal customer profile](https://blog.floworks.ai/ideal-customer-profile-template/) and a small sample of accounts. Include some companies you know well so you can check the output against what your team already knows. Review net-new prospects separately from customers and open opportunities.


### Ask what the signal actually contains


Choose a sample account and ask what signal the tool recorded, when it occurred, and what it means. A category visit, a topic surge, and a funding announcement each give you a different reason to investigate.


Find out how much source detail sellers can inspect. Some products provide modeled or aggregated activity without showing an individual browsing event. Check the information a rep will receive and whether a score comes with a public source link.


### Check account identity and contact identity separately


An account match tells you where to investigate. It does not automatically establish which employee performed the activity or who owns the purchase.


Have vendors show how they distinguish an observed account from a known or suggested contact. Your team needs a way to find a relevant person without assuming that person performed the anonymous research.


### Test the next action in your existing workflow


Give the vendor a task your team needs to complete, such as sending an account to its owner with enough context to review it. Have them demonstrate it using the package they have quoted.


Check how the system handles existing customers, open opportunities, and duplicate accounts. Decide who reviews new signals and what happens when an account is a poor fit. Assign responsibility for the marketing to sales handoff too.


### Compare the cost of the whole job


Base every quote on the same expected workload. Add up the subscription and required add-ons, including credit consumption and implementation work. Check for separate contact-data or export charges and confirm that the contract covers the products and regions you need.


During a pilot, count the accounts your team reviewed and those that gave sellers a specific, relevant action to take. Record “interesting signal” and “qualified opportunity” separately. A rep accepting an account for research is an earlier outcome than a prospect agreeing to a meeting.


If you compare signal-led accounts with another group, keep the segments and outreach conditions comparable. Use a small pilot to find workflow problems. Establishing a reliable revenue lift requires more evidence.


## Example: turning an account signal into a relevant conversation


The following is a fictional evaluation example, not a customer result.


A B2B SaaS company sells onboarding software to mid-sized employers. Its sales team receives a research alert for a target account. Separately, a public job posting says the company is hiring an employee onboarding manager.


The rep records the evidence and its limits:


Evidence What it supports What still needs checking


Account-level research about onboarding The company may be exploring the subject Who researched it and whether a project exists


Current onboarding-manager job posting The company is recruiting for a relevant role Whether the role owns software selection


Company matches the target segment It meets the team’s account criteria Its current process, constraints, and priorities


The rep checks the posting’s date and confirms the company match before choosing a contact. A possible opening is:


“I noticed your team is hiring an onboarding manager. Is standardizing onboarding across departments part of that role’s remit? We help HR teams manage that process, and I can share an example if it is relevant.”


The message references a verifiable public detail and gives the prospect room to explain whether the suspected need exists. The alert helped the rep prioritize the account. The conversation is where they learn about the business situation.


## Where Jesse fits alongside intent data tools


Jesse, a Floworks product, supports company and people research using the live web. Its site describes discovery using public activity such as hiring, funding announcements, conference attendance, and construction permits. It also offers role-based contact finding and enrichment. CSV export is available; the site currently lists native integrations as coming soon.[Jesse product information](https://agentjesse.ai/) .


This approach is worth considering when you want to investigate a visible company change. You might be looking for target accounts that are expanding, recruiting for a relevant role, or announcing a project.


Public events give you context to investigate. They do not establish a person’s private browsing activity, approved budget, or readiness to buy. Consider Jesse when you need that public context, including when you are researching an account flagged by another source.


[Book a Jesse demo](https://calendly.com/vivek-floworks/30min) with your target market and one public event you use to prioritize accounts. Ask to see how company discovery and contact selection work against those criteria, including the research context available to your team.


## Which intent data tool should you shortlist?


Choose your shortlist around the decision sellers need help making. If you need topic research across business websites, evaluate Bombora and the relevant data offerings from 6sense or Demandbase. For software evaluation activity, check G2’s coverage of your category. Existing HubSpot users should review the intent features and credit requirements available to them before adding another platform.


Pick two options that answer the same research question and give them the same account sample. Review the signals with a seller, then work through what they would do next. Before committing, document any coverage gaps and the full cost and requirements of the purchase.
